A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Discrete Guidance work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, code listings and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original guided-generation experiments on images, molecules, enhancer DNA and protein sequences in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical investigations and adds DiGress comparisons, broader exact-versus-approximate evaluations and additional protein case studies in Section 6 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The core predictor-guided and predictor-free rate formulas, Taylor approximation and fixed-state handling remain unchanged. However, v3 Appendix F.4.3 adds a second training stage for the stability-guidance predictor using generated samples labelled by the clean predictor, beyond the initial training described in v2.

E1.justification: The source datasets and four application domains remain; CIFAR-10 moves to Appendix F.1 rather than disappearing. Enhancer evaluation drops cell-type class 21, reducing nine evaluated classes across v2's main text and appendix to eight in v3 Appendix F.3.4. No new task family is introduced.

E2.justification: v3 evaluates DiGress against Discrete Guidance on molecules, enhancer DNA and proteins; v2 discussed DiGress without these empirical comparisons. GWG-Opt is removed from the protein comparisons. Dirichlet FM, ProteinMPNN and the unguided CTDD comparison remain.

E3.justification: The protein evaluation changes its sampling step size and structure-conditioning temperature, adds predictor training and expands from three to eight targets. The enhancer predictor-guidance strength grid also changes. Added experiments introduce DiGress protocols, molecular MAE and diversity evaluation, and enhancer success/diversity metrics. These changes prevent interpreting revised scores simply as same-setting improvements.

E4.justification: v2 compares exact and approximate guidance principally through molecular ring-count histograms. v3 extends this investigation across all three scientific applications, adds molecular diversity analyses and guidance-strength comparisons, and evaluates enhancer generation with alternative success/diversity metrics. Conversely, v2's image and enhancer noisy-classifier performance plots are removed.

E5.justification: v3 adds molecular MAE standard errors and Mann-Whitney tests, uncertainty for molecular validity, and five-bootstrap-replicate means and standard deviations for enhancer metrics. v2 already reported protein t-tests and qualitatively discussed seed variability, so this is a substantial expansion rather than the first statistical reporting. Bootstrap replicates do not establish additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: New molecular MAEs, enhancer comparisons and expanded protein tables substantially change the reported evidence. DG outperforms DiGress on molecules and generally on proteins, while performing comparably on enhancer DNA. The new 6ACV case favors TAG over exact guidance, with maximum success rates of 74% and 46% respectively (v3 Table 10). Protein results are revised under changed settings; CIFAR IS/FID and PDB recovery values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the score definition from the gradient of the density to the gradient of its logarithm. The guidance derivations, assumptions and fixed-state mathematics otherwise remain substantively unchanged. v3's separate generality subsection, C.8, largely reproduces material already in v2 C.7.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a general CTMC guidance framework and an efficient approximation. The headline application emphasis shifts toward scientific generation, and v2's claim of improved unconditional image generation is explicitly reframed in v3 Appendix F.1.2 as a check of conditional sample quality and distribution coverage.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning approximation error, predictor miscalibration and why exact guidance can sometimes perform worse than TAG. It qualifies FBD as a heuristic and adds explicit limitations about TAG's missing theoretical guarantees and uncertainty over predictor-training strategies. These substantially extend v2's predominantly proof-of-concept interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 adds DiGress implementation settings, predictor-retraining details and molecular fingerprint specifications while retaining most existing architectures and resource links. Reproducibility also suffers limited regressions: Listings 1 and 4 introduce inconsistent variable names, respectively pred_model versus model and guidance_strength versus inverse_guide_temp.

R1.justification: Targeted additions cover Gat et al.'s discrete flow matching, literature supporting gradient approximations, and preference-based fine-tuning in Appendix E.1. The DiGress contrast becomes more prominent, and the Emami reference associated with GWG-Opt disappears. The central positioning around CTMC guidance remains intact.

P1.justification: The empirical narrative and discussion are extensively rewritten, image modeling moves from the main experiments to the appendix, and Appendix F gains a detailed numbered subsection hierarchy. Guidance-strength terminology and exact/TAG naming become more systematic, while citations switch from numerical to author-year form. This exceeds local copyediting.

P2.justification: Molecular figures gain comparison and diversity panels; enhancer plots are consolidated and redesigned; and the main protein table is replaced by a comparative bar chart with expanded appendix tables. Image displays are relocated and noisy-classifier plots removed. Typography, captions and table formatting also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important empirical weakness in v2 by directly evaluating the closely related DiGress approach and testing exact versus approximate guidance beyond ring-count generation. The added diversity analyses, uncertainty reporting and explicit failure interpretations provide substantially stronger scrutiny of the framework. Broader protein testing strengthens support, although changed settings preclude simple cross-version performance claims. Removing GWG-Opt and classifier diagnostics, and introducing code-listing inconsistencies, are drawbacks, but they are outweighed by the stronger comparative evidence and clearer limitations.
